evidence.description: Project-scoped Screen Recording Settings popover for 'YT Long - How to buy wholesale for your store' shows Cursor Style = Pointer-first (previously Arrow-first)
textIncludes: YT Long - How to buy wholesale for your store

visualCheck.scope: Per-project "Screen Recording Settings" popover opened inside the draft "YT Long - How to buy wholesale for your store" (document-scope override), not Brand Kit → Screen Clips.
visualCheck.why: The frame shows the project-level Screen Recording Settings panel with Cursor Style set to "Pointer-first", matching the agent's claim of a per-project override; the brand-wide Brand Kit surface is not open and thus untouched.

summary:
I changed the cursor type for just one project, using the DOCUMENT-scope override rather than the brand default — because the task explicitly says "just this one project, without affecting other projects", and Brand Kit → Screen Clips would have changed the default for every project on the brand.

Steps performed: opened the draft "YT Long - How to buy wholesale for your store" from the sidebar → clicked the Project actions (⋯) button next to the voice picker → chose "Screen Clip Settings…" (the per-project "Screen Recording Settings" popover) → opened the Cursor Style combobox (was "Arrow-first") → selected "Pointer-first" (my chosen value, since the task didn't name one) → clicked Done to commit.

Verified by reopening Project actions ⋯ → Screen Clip Settings…: the popover now reads Cursor Style = Pointer-first, with no trace of Arrow-first, confirming the value was saved on this project only. The brand-wide Brand Kit → Screen Clips setting was deliberately left untouched.
